title: Trying to learn game dev through AI prototyping instead of tutorials.
author: darkluna_94
selftext:
I’m trying to learn game development in a different way this year. Instead of following tutorials, I want to build a bunch of tiny, playable games to learn by doing. I’ve been experimenting with tools like [Tessala.co](https://tessala.co/) to quickly spin up mechanics and see what actually works when played. The focus isn’t on polish, story, or visuals, just making small, interactive ideas that can be finished quickly.

For people who’ve worked with AI assisted game workflows before, what kinds of game concepts tend to work best in this kind of rapid prototyping? I’m especially curious about games that stay fun even when minimal and can realistically be built in just a few days.

comments.author: Unique-Painting-9364
comments.body: Learning by building is honestly the fastest way small playable projects teach you way more than tutorials ever will. Looks like a fun path.
